Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the intro. Attached is our initial draft of a Model Exchange / Distribution agreement (OpenEcho_Model_Exchange_Draft_v1.docx) that lays out: access mechanics for weights, redistribution rights, attribution, and a proposed rev-share framework.

High level asks from our side:
- We want clarity on how Redwood will make model weights available to downstream ISV partners (S3 presigned vs. mirrored repository).
- Redistribution tiers: what constitutes "redistribution" vs. "inference-only access" for downstream tooling partners.
- Embargo and versioning controls; ability to revoke access for security fixes.
- A basic pilot structure (non-exclusive) so we can validate telemetry/attribution before a broader rollout.

Can your team confirm who owns the operational workflow for onboarding a publisher (ingest, metadata, validation) vs. who handles legal/contract redlines? We can join a quick call this week to align.

Attaching the draft for your review.

Thanks Matthew — appreciate the thoughtful draft. We're excited to explore a distribution channel with OpenEcho.

Quick answers up front:
- Operational split: Partnerships (me + Camila) take ownership for go-to-market, partner onboarding, and pricing tiers. Redwood Legal (cc'd in follow ups) will lead contract negotiations and redlines.
- We prefer presigned S3 URLs for initial pilots (simpler audit trail), with the option to mirror packages into a controlled repo for larger, production rollouts.
- For redistribution vs inference-only, we typically differentiate by whether downstreams receive binary weight files versus an API/SDK-only integration. We'll propose a three-tier model.

Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow (Thu) at 11:00 PT? If that works, I'll loop in Jonas (partnerships ops) and Laura (legal) afterwards.

On Wed, Jul 30, 2025 at 10:03 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Matthew — appreciate the thoughtful draft. We're excited to explore a distribution channel with OpenEcho.

Matthew / Sergio - looping in operational detail we should consider up front so Legal and Eng have a clear starting point. High-level suggestions below (short, actionable).

Access & bandwidth model (ops):
- Pilot: presigned S3 URLs, time-limited keys, per-model object manifests. Only publisher and Redwood have write access; partners receive read-only links.
- Production: mirrored model repo with signed provenance metadata and digest checks.
- Usage telemetry: imprint unique partner token in inference headers for attribution; clearly document token lifecycle.

License / contract clauses to prioritize (legal):
- Redistribution vs inference-only: redistribution = delivery of model binaries or converted weights. Inference-only = API/SDK calling without weights transfer.
- Attribution: require a standardized model attribution header and a short credit in product UIs.
- Embargo & revocation: 14-day notice for non-security revocations; immediate revocation for live-issue/security incidents.
- Escrow & escrow triggers: offer an escrow option (third-party vault) for high-value models tied to revenue thresholds.

Operational checklist (ops owners):
- Provide model manifest (name, version, checksum, license), README, evaluation harness.
- Define acceptance tests (latency, safety surface) and rollout gating (canary -> batch -> full).
- Tagging scheme: publisher_id, model_family, quantization_profile, provenance_hash.

For the pilot, suggest: 3 models, 90-day pilot, non-exclusive, Redwood runs attribution telemetry and reports weekly. Rev-share is negotiable — we can start conversation at 20% and adjust by volume/portal contribution.

I attached the ingest schema we use for publisher onboarding (ingest_schema_v2.json) — helps surface required fields.

Attachments: ingest_schema_v2.json (4KB)

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Camila / Sergio — this is very helpful, thank you.

We're aligned on the pilot structure. A couple of asks from OpenEcho Legal/Compliance:
- SOC 2 letter or equivalent attestation on telemetry handling.
- Data retention window for any telemetry/usage logs (we'd like 90 days by default).
- Confirmation we won't be required to distribute source model checkpoints beyond presigned objects unless explicitly agreed.

Proposed pilot commercial terms (initial):
- Scope: 3 models, 90 days, non-exclusive pilot
- Rev-share: 20% of net revenue attributable to redistributors that use OpenEcho models via Redwood channels
- Attribution: mandatory header + weekly report (Redwood provides partner attribution CSV)

I'll start the DocuSign envelope with our basic Master Partner Addendum (link below) so Legal can mark redlines. CEO and Legal are reviewing now — Arielle (cc'd) is our legal point.
